places.name: Te Toto Gorge
places.description: Follow the wild west coast to a dramatic lookout above the Tasman Sea. Towering cliffs, green hills and a spectacular volcanic landscape make this one of the most memorable viewpoints near Raglan. Stop for photos, enjoy the sea air and take in the sweeping coastline.
places.note: Whaanga Road includes gravel sections. Confirm that the route and rental conditions permit this trip.

places.name: Whale Bay
places.description: A quieter coastal spot famous for its rocky shoreline and long left-hand surf breaks. Watch experienced surfers from a safe vantage point and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere of this small seaside community.
places.note: Rocky coast and powerful surf; not a beginner swimming beach.

places.name: Manu Bay
places.description: One of Raglan’s iconic surf locations, known for beautiful left-hand waves and its place in surf history. Find a spot overlooking the point, watch surfers glide along the waves and see the working boat ramp.
places.note: Stay clear of boat-ramp traffic and slippery rocks.

places.name: Ngarunui Beach
places.description: Raglan’s sweeping black-sand beach is ideal for long walks, surf lessons and sunsets. Enjoy the viewpoints above the sand before heading down to the shore and taking in the vast Tasman Sea.
places.note: Swim between the flags when lifeguards are on patrol.

places.name: Jurassic Reserve
places.description: Enjoy the lush, almost prehistoric feel of Raglan’s coastal vegetation. This stop celebrates the wild green landscapes beside the surf coast.
places.note: Working map name: confirm the official location and public access before publishing.

places.name: The Reef
places.description: Watch swells roll across the rocky reefs that help give Raglan its celebrated surf. A scenic stop for ocean lovers and wave photography.
places.note: Confirm the intended reef and a safe, publicly accessible viewpoint.

places.name: Kitesurf Beach
places.description: On windy days, colourful kites add excitement to the water. Watch riders harness the wind while enjoying the open coastal scenery.
places.note: Confirm the actual launch and viewing area; keep clear of kites and lines.

places.name: Wainui Reserve Bush Park
places.description: Trade the ocean breeze for a sheltered walk among native plants and trees. Listen for birds, enjoy the greenery and take a refreshing nature break from the coast.
places.note: Confirm trail access and secure bikes only where parking is permitted.

places.name: The Skatepark
places.description: Stop by the skatepark to watch local riders, enjoy the harbour-side atmosphere and explore nearby green spaces. It is a fun contrast to the surf beaches further along the coast.

places.name: The Airstrip
places.description: A distinctive local landmark close to the coast. Enjoy the surrounding open landscape and, if you are lucky, catch a glimpse of light aircraft from a safe public area.
places.note: Active aerodrome: do not enter operational areas or cross the runway.

places.name: SunCamel
places.description: Your starting point for a memorable Raglan ride. Pick up your SunCamel e-bike, get comfortable with the controls and set off to discover the coast, harbour and town.
places.note: Confirm pickup instructions and times when booking.

places.name: Raglan Town
places.description: Raglan’s lively village centre is full of independent cafés, creative shops and laid-back surf culture. Stop for coffee, browse local art and enjoy the atmosphere of this friendly coastal town.

places.name: The Wharf
places.description: Explore Raglan’s working waterfront, with fishing boats, harbour views and places to grab a bite. Take your time, watch the boats and soak up the maritime character of Whāingaroa.

places.name: Rangitahi
places.description: Discover a peaceful peninsula surrounded by tidal estuary waters. Ride through the neighbourhood on public roads, enjoy the open spaces and admire the changing light across the harbour.
